title: Pentaho BI Developer - SW Practitioner
description: Hands-on workshop for the OLAP / Mondrian schema BI Developer. Build, extend, and publish Mondrian schemas with Pentaho Schema Workbench — cubes, dimensions, hierarchies, levels, measures, calculated members, named sets — and query them with MDX.

moduleSummaries.title: Getting Started
moduleSummaries.summary: OLAP vs. OLTP, multidimensional cubes, star vs. normalized schemas, and the ROLAP Mondrian engine — the mental model behind every hands-on lab that follows.

moduleSummaries.title: Schemas
moduleSummaries.summary: The building blocks of a Mondrian schema, then three guided builds against the SteelWheels SampleData: explore the prebuilt SteelWheels cube, build the Classic Models schema step by step, then prove your skills by constructing the Miniature Models schema independently.

moduleSummaries.title: Extend Model
moduleSummaries.summary: Take a basic cube to production grade: shared time dimensions, geographic annotations for maps, member properties, degenerate dimensions, and calculated members (UnitPrice, Top 10 Customers) that embed business logic in the semantic layer.

moduleSummaries.title: MDX Query
moduleSummaries.summary: Query cubes directly with MDX to validate and troubleshoot your schemas — SELECT / FROM / WHERE, axes vs. slicers, member references — then centralise reusable member collections with Named Sets.

moduleSummaries.title: Data Security
moduleSummaries.summary: Lock cubes down with Mondrian's role-based security: roles and role mappers, then the grant hierarchy (Schema, Cube, Hierarchy, Member) and rollup policies, applied hands-on as four progressively restrictive roles on the Miniature Models schema.

moduleSummaries.title: Localization
moduleSummaries.summary: Serve a global audience from a single schema. Tokenize the Classic Models schema, deploy English and French property files, and configure Mondrian's dynamic schema processor so cubes translate automatically by user locale.
